edge_cases: Missing required form fields may cause a server error or a generic 400 response.
Attempting to register with an existing username triggers a redirect to /login instead of creating a duplicate record.
Login with an incorrect password or non‑existent username returns "Invalid credentials".
Creating a project for a username that does not exist returns "User not found".
Adding a task to a project name that does not exist returns "Project not found".
Viewing tasks for a project with no associated tasks returns an empty JSON array.
contract.intent: Expose a web API that lets clients register and authenticate users, create projects, add tasks to projects, and retrieve tasks for a given project.
invariants: Usernames are unique; a second registration with the same username never creates a new record.
Passwords are never stored in plain text; they are stored as SHA‑256(salt || password).
Each task must reference an existing project; tasks are only added after the project existence check.
Each project must reference an existing user; projects are only created after the user existence check.
The salt for each user is stored as a hex string and used for password verification.
All database writes are committed only after successful validation checks.
io_behavior: POST /register with username and password returns a redirect to /login on duplicate usernames or the text "Registration successful" on success.
POST /login with username and password returns a redirect to /dashboard on valid credentials or the text "Invalid credentials" otherwise.
POST /project/create with username and project_name returns "Project created successfully" if the user exists, otherwise "User not found".
POST /task/add with project_name, task_name, and task_description returns "Task added successfully" if the project exists, otherwise "Project not found".
GET /tasks/view?project_name=... returns a JSON array of {task_name, task_description} objects for the specified project.
side_effects: Inserts a new user record (username, hashed password, salt, account_created flag) into the users table.
Inserts a new project record (username, project_name) into the projects table.
Inserts a new task record (project_name, task_name, task_description) into the tasks table.
Updates the MySQL database with each successful insert and commits the transaction.
Issues HTTP redirects (307) to /login or /dashboard as part of the response flow.

rationale: Program implements most API routes and edge‑case handling correctly, but stores passwords using Werkzeug’s hash instead of SHA‑256 with a stored salt and returns a different success message on registration, violating key invariants and exact I/O semantics.
